newsitem.title: UK: British Gas says Ofgas review was "flawed".
newsitem.headline: British Gas says Ofgas review was "flawed".

text.p: British Gas Plc chairman Richard Giordano said on Thursday that regulatory body Ofgas's approach to price control proposals for its TransCo gas trasnmission business was "flawed."
"It has been a flawed process," Giordano told Reuters Financial Television after British Gas rejected the proposals.

"We have not had access to consultants' reports, for example, that underpin Ofgas's decisions. It is quite an unusual event to have the foundation of these decisions not subjected to scrutiny by those who have to implement them."
Giordano said he was confident that the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), now expected to conduct a lengthy inquiry into the price controls, would back British Gas.
"We believe we will get a very careful scrutiny of the whole subject by the MMC which we have not had so far," he said.

But he warned that if the MMC upheld Ofgas's price proposals "there will be a diminished reward for shareholders, there will be less resource to sustain the system, and I think if we are in any way to achieve the cost targets which Ofgas is setting there will be job losses."

Giordano declined to be drawn on what level of price cuts British Gas would find acceptable for TransCo, although he said it would not be "a level at all close" to the 20 percent one-off cut and subsequent four-year price cap of 6.5 percent below inflation proposed by Ofgas regulator Clare Spottiswoode.
He supported the view of deputy chairman Philip Rogerson that the MMC inquiry will not affect the planned demerger of British Gas's U.K. supply business, British Gas Energy, early next year.
He predicted that it would probably be accomplished "before we even get an outcome from the MMC."
